item.title: Large Language Models (LLMs) for Tourism and Tourists
item.content:encoded:
This special issue invites submissions exploring the applications, implications, and innovations of Large Language Models (LLMs) in the tourism industry and for enhancing tourist experiences. The rapidly evolving landscape of artificial intelligence presents unprecedented opportunities and challenges for tourism stakeholders, from destination management organizations to hospitality providers to individual travelers.

Appel publié par Annals of Tourism Research. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Applications of LLMs in tourism management and operations
  • LLMs for personalized tourist experiences and recommendations
  • Natural language processing applications in tourism marketing
  • LLMs for tourism chatbots and customer service
  • Language translation and communication in tourism contexts
  • LLMs for travel planning and itinerary generation
  • Sentiment analysis and tourist feedback analysis using LLMs
  • LLMs for tourism research and data analysis

Timeline

  • August 31, 2026: Full paper submission deadline

item.title: Large Language Models (LLMs) for Tourism and Tourists
item.content:encoded:
This special issue focuses on the applications and implications of Large Language Models (LLMs) in the tourism sector. We invite research exploring how LLMs can enhance tourist experiences, improve tourism service delivery, and support both tourism businesses and individual travelers. The issue welcomes empirical studies, theoretical frameworks, case studies, and critical analyses of LLM technologies in tourism contexts.

item.title: Large Language Models as Methodological Innovators: Advancing Theory and Practice in Technology Management
item.content:encoded:
This special issue seeks to explore how Large Language Models (LLMs) are transforming methodological approaches in technology management research. We invite submissions that demonstrate innovative applications of LLMs as research tools, methodological enhancers, and theoretical instruments for advancing our understanding of technology management, innovation, and organizational change.

Contributions should address both the opportunities and challenges of incorporating LLMs into research practice, including questions of validity, reliability, ethical considerations, and the development of new theoretical frameworks that account for LLM capabilities and limitations in research contexts.

Appel publié par Technological Forecasting and Social Change. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Applications of LLMs in technology management research
  • LLMs for data analysis and pattern recognition in technology studies
  • Novel methodological approaches enabled by LLMs
  • Theoretical frameworks for understanding LLM capabilities and limitations in research contexts
  • LLMs for literature review and synthesis
  • LLM-assisted qualitative and quantitative research methods
  • Validation and reliability of LLM-based research findings
  • Ethical considerations in using LLMs for academic research
  • LLMs for forecasting technological trends
  • Integration of LLMs with traditional research methodologies

Timeline

  • January 1, 2027: Submission deadline

item.title: Generative AI and LLM in financial modelling and applications
item.content:encoded:
Steve Yang, Stevens Institute of Technology

Jing Chen, Cardiff University

Aparna Gupta, Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute

Zachary Feinstein, Stevens Institute of Technology

William Knottenbelt, Imperial College

This special issue aims to explore the specific financial modelling issues related to Artificial Intelligence (AI), in particular Generative AI and Large Language models (LLMs) modelling and applications in finance. It seeks to offer new insights in consideration of Generative AI/LLM innovation that brings changes to the traditional finance topics such as asset pricing, financial intermediation, financial markets & investment, behavioural finance, banking, accounting, insurance, etc. The special issue particularly encourages work that advances the understanding of how Gen AI and LLM modelling brings forward ethical implications, benefits financial inclusion and/or enhances regulatory and policy changes.

Appel publié par The European Journal of Finance. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Asset pricing with Generative AI and LLMs
  • Financial intermediation applications of Generative AI and LLMs
  • Financial markets and investment strategies using Generative AI and LLMs
  • Behavioural finance and AI applications
  • Banking and AI applications
  • Accounting and AI applications
  • Insurance and AI applications
  • Ethical implications of Generative AI and LLMs in finance
  • Financial inclusion through Generative AI and LLMs
  • Regulatory and policy changes driven by AI in finance
  • Data generation and analysis using Generative AI
  • Risk management with Generative AI and LLMs
  • FinBERT and finance-focused language models
  • Data privacy concerns in AI-driven finance
  • Cost reduction through AI predictions while managing innovation

Timeline

  • September 15, 2026: Manuscript deadline

item.title: The Agentic Supply Chain: Entering a new era in AI in Supply Chain Management
item.content:encoded:
Alexandra Brintrup, University of Cambridge

Thomas Choi, Arizona State University

George Huang, Hong Kong Polytechnic University

Dmitry Ivanov, Berlin School of Economics and Law

Recent advances in Agentic Large Language Models (LLMs) are reshaping the discourse on how autonomous decision systems might operate in complex environments such as supply chains. The motivation for the special issue is to facilitate rigorous research in the transformative potential of agentic technology for Supply Chain Management (SCM). A key objective is to foster collaboration and unlock synergies by merging diverse perspectives from operations and supply chain management, AI, complexity science, and industrial engineering.

An AI agent is characterised as one that has a predefined or emergent goal and uses cognitive tools to achieve its objectives, such as situational awareness, data-driven learning and prediction, decision optimisation, negotiation, and problem-solving with human or other AI agents. Supply chain management scholars have long studied agent-based systems, especially multi-agent systems (MAS) since the 2000s. However, research has stalled as MAS were slow to develop, difficult to code, debug and scale, and were prone to severe coordination problems. Most supply chain agent research was not adopted in the industry.

Appel publié par International Journal of Production Research. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Discourse on utilising agentic systems for complex scenarios in supply chain management: Risk and disruption management, logistics and supply chain optimisation, transportation routes, inventory management, quality control, demand forecasting, and warehouse planning and location, and cash flow predictions
  • Supply network design with agentic technology: Supplier relationship configurations, agentic digital twins to simulate inventory flows, sustainability implications across the supply chain, circular supply chains, supply chain visibility, and supply chain financing
  • Interorganisational agentic systems: Effective multi-agent negotiation and coordination, the design of mediative and persuasive agentic systems, preservation of organisational privacy during multi-agent communication
  • Hybrid systems: Integration of agentic systems with blockchain, IoT, Omniverse, and traditional multi-agent systems
  • Emergence and Complexity: Unintended consequences of agentic deployment at the system scale, governance, trustworthiness and safety, centralised versus decentralised control, human-in-the-loop agentic systems
  • Technical challenges: Performance evaluation, efficient task division, ablation analysis and back testing, sensitivity analysis, agentic architectures operating in high uncertainty environments, long-term horizon reasoning, overcoming hallucinations

Timeline

  • September 30, 2026: Manuscript deadline
